what_its_for: This medicine helps lower high potassium levels in your blood. High potassium (called hyperkalemia) can be dangerous for your heart. This medicine works by trapping extra potassium in your gut and removing it from your body through your bowel movements.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a powder you mix with water or as a liquid suspension. You can take it by mouth or it can be given as an enema (through your rectum). If taking by mouth, mix the powder with water or a non-citrus juice as directed. Do NOT mix with orange juice or other citrus juices. Drink it slowly. If given as an enema, a nurse or caregiver will help you with this. Do not take this medicine with laxatives that contain sorbitol, as this combination can be very dangerous. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's exact instructions.
dosing: Adults usually take 15 grams (about 4 level teaspoons of powder) one to four times a day by mouth. The exact dose depends on your potassium level and your doctor's instructions. For an enema, the typical adult dose is 30 to 50 grams given every 6 hours. Do not take more or less than your doctor prescribed. Each dose of the powder should be mixed with at least 3 to 4 tablespoons (45 mL) of water.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store the powder at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. If you have the pre-mixed liquid suspension, store it in the refrigerator and use it within the time frame listed on the label. Do not freeze the liquid form. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine properly — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking this medicine with laxatives or antacids that contain magnesium or calcium (such as Milk of Magnesia or Maalox), as they can reduce how well this medicine works and may cause serious problems. Do not mix the powder with orange juice, other citrus juices, or any liquid that contains a lot of potassium. Avoid foods very high in potassium (such as bananas, oranges, potatoes, and tomatoes) unless your doctor says otherwise. Do not take other oral medicines within 3 hours of taking this medicine, as it may prevent them from being absorbed properly. Ask your pharmacist about specific medicines to separate.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: severe stomach pain, cramps, or bloating; no bowel movement after taking the medicine for more than a few days; bloody or black stools; nausea or vomiting that will not stop; signs of low potassium such as muscle weakness, cramps, irregular heartbeat, or extreme tiredness; signs of low calcium such as muscle spasms, numbness, or tingling; difficulty breathing; or swelling of your stomach that is getting worse. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or if you feel your potassium levels are not being controlled.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working within 2 to 12 hours when taken by mouth. It may take a bit longer when given as an enema. Your doctor will check your blood potassium levels regularly to see how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep all lab appointments so your doctor can adjust your dose if needed.
special_populations: Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as low potassium, low magnesium, or constipation. Close monitoring is recommended. Kidney disease patients: This medicine is often used in people with kidney disease, but careful monitoring of blood electrolytes (potassium, sodium, calcium) is very important since the kidneys are already not working well. Patients with heart failure or high blood pressure: Be cautious because this medicine contains sodium, which can cause fluid retention or worsen these conditions. Talk to your doctor about the risks. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medicine. The safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Children: This medicine can be used in children, but only under strict medical supervision with carefully calculated doses based on the child's weight. Patients with bowel problems: This medicine should be used with caution or avoided in people who have reduced bowel movement, bowel obstruction, or have recently had bowel surgery, as it can worsen these conditions.
